category_feedback.specific_evidence: Lesson 1 names C3.1 and the activities target it, but the lesson_overview / minds_on / consolidation never bridge to neighbouring days. The expanded_walkthrough does not cross-reference Lesson 2's writing or Lesson 3's reading-and-tracing — it ends at 'every IF-THEN reading task starts with check the condition first' without naming the next day.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add explicit forward/backward bridges in teacher_script. In consolidation, plant a hook for Lesson 2 like: 'Tomorrow Then the Action Dog will help us WRITE our own IF-THEN code for math — even/odd, big/small. Today we read; tomorrow we write.' In the expanded_walkthrough name the gating reflex as the foundation Lessons 2-4 will build on.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough names a real Grade-2 trap (always-true / 'action runs every time') with concrete recovery (2-step routine, sentence frame, mixed inputs). However recovery_moves do NOT branch by diagnostic, and no research is cited (no Bers/ScratchJr conditional research, no Kazakoff & Bers, no Flannery & Bers on conditionals).
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite a named source for the always-true misconception (e.g., Bers 2018 on conditional reasoning in early coding, or Kazakoff/Bers ScratchJr studies). Branch recovery_moves: if the child can articulate TRUE/FALSE but still acts → drill the gate; if the child cannot decide TRUE/FALSE for the input → drop back to TRUE/FALSE labelling on the truth chart before re-introducing the gate.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Inspector If anchors minds_on, action, and consolidation, and success_criteria all use 'I can'. But there is NO distinctive quotable refrain — consolidation 'Inspector If's IF-THEN Brag' uses generic discussion prompts and a sticky-note exit, with no chant or sentence frame children carry between lessons. Compare the rubric's L4 example 'HOO knows the sounds? YOU do!'.
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Inspector If a memorable refrain children chant back at every consolidation, e.g., 'CHECK the IF — THEN do the THEN!' Add it explicitly to consolidation.exit_routine and have the teacher_script close the minds_on with it, so it reappears in Lessons 2-5 as a unit-wide chant.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Worksheet Parts 1-3 each map to a named success criterion and materials match. But the worksheet is essentially a rote restatement of station work (find IF/THEN, decide TRUE/FALSE, write own) — it does NOT deliberately vary the practice format as a transfer task, and there is no justified Part-3 generalization probe with unfamiliar contexts.
category_feedback.required_fix: Vary at least one part as a transfer task and justify it in teacher_notes. E.g., reframe Part 2 so two of the four rows use UNFAMILIAR conditions (e.g., 'IF the day ends in y, THEN smile' — silly transfer) to verify the gating generalizes; or add a Part-3 prompt requiring one math IF-THEN AND one real-life IF-THEN to probe transfer beyond station examples.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Conceptual progression is explicit (condition→check→action; TRUE/FALSE gates the action) and vocabulary is precise. But children do not invent or compare strategies — Station C asks them to write their own IF-THEN with no compare move, and expanded_walkthrough names the trap only colloquially (no Bers, no CGI-style framing).
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a compare-strategies micro-discussion to the action phase or consolidation: surface two children's invented IF-THENs (one with a math condition, one with a real-life condition) and have the class trace both with the same input, then discuss which condition was easier to check and why. Cite Bers (2018) or equivalent in expanded_walkthrough.rationale to ground the always-true trap.

summary: Pair 1 is solid Level-3 work across the board with one Level-4 (instructional_balance: optional puppets, body-based movement differentiation, realistic 12/25/13 timing). To clear the strict pass bar the lesson needs (a) a quotable Inspector-If refrain children carry into Lessons 2-5, (b) named research grounding the always-true trap with diagnostic-branched recovery, (c) explicit forward/backward bridging language; and the worksheet needs a justified transfer-task variation (unfamiliar conditions or required real-life vs math contrast in Part 3) rather than a rote restatement of station work.
